name: WCRP vulnerability, overall: original 2022 (index and level by barrio)
plain: How vulnerable each barrio was in all six areas together compared with the other barrios, in the WCRP Risk and Vulnerability Indicators as published in 2022: a level from 1 (the least vulnerable fifth) to 5 (the most vulnerable fifth).
definition: The overall index of the Risk and Vulnerability Indicators (RVI) that Hunter College built for Foundation for Puerto Rico's Whole Community Resilience Planning (WCRP) program, as published in March 2022: the barrio's percentile among the 887 barrios with residents (0 to 1 in the source, stored times 100), where higher is more vulnerable, and its rank, the fifth of the index (1 = 0 to 20, low; 5 = above 80, high). Inputs: the six area indices (economy, education, environment, health, housing, infrastructure), with equal weights. Mostly ACS 2015-2019; the environment inputs are EPA layers of about 2021 and FPR-supplied waste layers, travel time to a hospital was computed by Hunter College, and intersection density uses TIGER 2020. The 14 barrios with no residents or structures have no value.
unit: percentile among barrios (0 to 100); rank 1 to 5

coverage.frequency: Published once (March 2022); wcrp_rvi.py reads the public services again on request

method: Read as published from the public ArcGIS service All_Indicator (the OVERALL row of each barrio carries every area's index and rank); nothing is recomputed. The build checks that each published rank is the fifth of the published index (rank = ceil(5 x index), at least 1) and stops if one is not. Method of the source (white paper, December 2021): each input becomes a percentile among the barrios, the percentiles of an area are added and the sum ranked again; the overall index ranks the sum of the six area indices. Applied to the original's own published inputs, that method gives back this index with a rank correlation of 1.00 (99.8% of barrios keep their rank).
source_detail: ArcGIS REST service All_Indicator (account PlanningCDBG), fields OVERALL, OVERA_RANK
how_to_read: Read the rank, not small differences in the index: each rank holds a fifth of the barrios (about 177). Compare groups of barrios; the barrio values of the survey behind most inputs are rough.
caveats: A rank compares barrios with each other on the inputs used. It is not a measure of need, risk of harm or eligibility for any program.

Foundation for Puerto Rico runs WCRP in collaboration with the Puerto Rico Department of Housing (PRDOH), with HUD CDBG-DR funds. The WCRP page is published with an 'In review' marker: these values may change, and the page asks search engines not to index it while the marker is on.

No open license is stated: the ArcGIS services publish no license or access terms. FPR publishes the values on the observatory with the program's approval; others should ask PRDOH and FPR before re-using them.
The dashboard's municipio and Puerto Rico comparison columns are mislabelled and some municipio lead-paint values exceed 100%; the barrio values used here are labelled correctly (see the WCRP page).

name: WCRP vulnerability, overall: updated 2020–2024 (index and level by barrio)
plain: The same ranking of barrios in all six areas together, updated by the observatory with the WCRP method on the Census survey of 2020–2024 and current local conditions (EPA sites, impaired waters and polluted air, severe housing problems, street intersections and the drive time to a hospital): a level from 1 (the least vulnerable fifth) to 5 (the most vulnerable fifth).
definition: The overall index of the Risk and Vulnerability Indicators rebuilt by the observatory with the white paper's method on American Community Survey 5-year estimates 2020–2024 and, for the environment, health, housing and infrastructure areas, the observatory's current local conditions (conditions_barrio.json): the barrio's percentile among the barrios with residents in that window, times 100 (higher is more vulnerable), and its rank, the fifth of the index. Inputs: the six area indices (economy, education, environment, health, housing, infrastructure), with equal weights. Computed from the six rebuilt areas, with equal weights.
unit: percentile among barrios (0 to 100); rank 1 to 5

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt by python wcrp_rvi.py; the next window (2021-2025) is due in December 2026

method: wcrp_rvi.py: each input becomes a percentile among the barrios that have a value (the share of them with a strictly lower value); within an area (or a sub-indicator: infrastructure's telecommunications and transportation; housing is the plain sum of its three inputs, which is what gives back the original) the percentiles are added and the sum ranked again; a barrio that lacks an input gets the sum of the inputs it has scaled to the full count (the white paper's education rule, generalised); the overall index ranks the sum of the six areas; the rank is ceil(5 x index), at least 1. A barrio with no residents in the window has no value. Inputs come from acs_barrio.json and, for public assistance (B19057), year built (B25034), computers (B28003), broadband (B28002) and school enrollment (B14003), from the same ACS window read by acs_small.py. The environment, hospital, severe housing problems and street inputs come from conditions_barrio.json (conditions.py: EPA TRI, Facility Registry Service, ATTAINS, Green Book and LMOP; HUD CHAS 2016-2020 spread from tracts; TIGER/Line 2026; drive time to a CMS general hospital along OpenStreetMap roads), each in its source's vintage. Against the original, 68% of the 879 barrios ranked in both change rank and 29% move two ranks or more (rank correlation 0.50).
source_detail: ACS 5-year 2020–2024, barrio rows (acs_barrio.json and tables B19057, B25034, B28003, B28002, B14003); method of the RVI white paper (Hunter College, 2021); conditions_barrio.json (EPA TRI, FRS, ATTAINS, Green Book, LMOP; HUD CHAS 2016-2020; TIGER/Line 2026; CMS hospitals and OpenStreetMap roads)
how_to_read: Read the rank, not small differences in the index. Where the rank differs from the original, the cause can be the inputs left out, five years of change or the roughness of barrio survey estimates: the WCRP page measures each.
caveats: A rank compares barrios with each other on the inputs used. It is not a measure of need, risk of harm or eligibility for any program.

Foundation for Puerto Rico runs WCRP in collaboration with the Puerto Rico Department of Housing (PRDOH), with HUD CDBG-DR funds. The WCRP page is published with an 'In review' marker: these values may change, and the page asks search engines not to index it while the marker is on.
Margins of error of the inputs are not carried into the index; barrio survey estimates are rough, so a barrio near the edge of a fifth can change rank between survey windows.

Inputs are defined from the ACS tables named in the method; the original does not say which cells it used, so a definition can differ (households without a computer average 62% of households per barrio in the original and 20% here).

Vieques, Culebra and Isla de Mona have no road to a general hospital and no drive time: their health index uses disability and health insurance only (the missing-input rule), which leaves out how far they are from hospital care.

plain: The same ranking of barrios in environment, updated by the observatory with the WCRP method on the Census survey of 2020–2024 and current EPA data on regulated sites, impaired waters and polluted air: a level from 1 (the least vulnerable fifth) to 5 (the most vulnerable fifth).
definition: The environment index of the Risk and Vulnerability Indicators rebuilt by the observatory with the white paper's method on American Community Survey 5-year estimates 2020–2024 and the observatory's current local conditions: the barrio's percentile among the barrios with residents in that window, times 100 (higher is more vulnerable), and its rank, the fifth of the index. Inputs: Lead-paint indicator: homes built before 1960 (%); In a sulfur dioxide or lead non-attainment area (1 = yes); In a 303(d)-listed water assessment unit, EPA ATTAINS (1 = yes); Risk Management Plan facilities, active (count); Municipal solid waste landfill, open or closed, EPA LMOP (1 = yes); Superfund (National Priorities List) sites (count); Toxics Release Inventory facilities (count). Left out because no current source states terms: Solid waste facilities (transfer stations, recycling, open dumps) (No public source states terms: EPA lists municipal landfills only, and the only list of open dumps found (DRNA, 2014) states no license.). Defined differently from the original: In a sulfur dioxide or lead non-attainment area (1 = yes): Areas still in non-attainment in the EPA Green Book: San Juan and Guayama-Salinas for sulfur dioxide, Arecibo for lead. In a 303(d)-listed water assessment unit, EPA ATTAINS (1 = yes): Puerto Rico maps the assessment units of its rivers as the land that drains to each assessed reach, so a listed unit covers a watershed and far more barrios touch one than in the original, which does not say how it drew the waters. The input separates barrios less than the original's. Risk Management Plan facilities, active (count): Only the facilities the Facility Registry Service marks active are counted, far fewer than the original counted; it does not say which it took. Municipal solid waste landfill, open or closed, EPA LMOP (1 = yes): EPA's Landfill Methane Outreach Program lists municipal solid waste landfills only (open or closed), not open dumps; the original's landfill or open dump layer was supplied by FPR.

name: WCRP Risk and Vulnerability Indicators: method, updated version and checks
plain: How the WCRP vulnerability index ranks barrios: each input becomes a percentile among barrios, the percentiles of an area are added and ranked again, the six areas are added for the overall index, and levels are fifths.
definition: Hunter College built the Risk and Vulnerability Indicators (RVI) for Foundation for Puerto Rico's Whole Community Resilience Planning (WCRP) program (white paper, December 2021; data published March 2022). Steps: (1) each input becomes a percentile among the barrios with a value, higher meaning more vulnerable; (2) within an area the percentiles are added and the sum ranked again (infrastructure through two sub-indicators; the white paper describes two for housing too, but the published housing index is the plain sum of its inputs); (3) the overall index ranks the sum of the six area indices with equal weights; (4) ranks are fifths: 1 = 0 to 0.20 (low) to 5 = above 0.80 (high). Barrios with no residents have no value; in education, 21 barrios with nobody aged 3 to 24 have their no-diploma percentile doubled. The observatory shows the original as published and a rebuild on ACS 2020–2024 and its current local conditions (conditions_barrio.json). Input left out of the rebuild: Solid waste facilities (transfer stations, recycling, open dumps) (environment).
unit: not applicable (method)

coverage.frequency: Fixed by the white paper; the rebuild follows each new ACS window

method: The percentile that reproduces the original from its own inputs is the share of barrios with a strictly lower value (n = barrios with a value). With it, the original's own inputs give back its published index with rank correlation 1.00 for overall, education, health, housing and infrastructure; economy (0.68) and environment (0.93) do not reproduce. Housing reproduces as a flat sum of its three inputs (1.00), not as the two sub-indicators the white paper describes (0.96). A hypothesis to confirm with Hunter College: the published economy index matches one built from public assistance, poverty and per capita income, with higher income counted as more vulnerable and without unemployment, much better (rank correlation 0.93, 81% same rank). Where the rebuild differs: ranking the original's 2015-2019 values with the rebuild's inputs changes 29% of overall ranks (almost all through economy and environment); the rebuild changes the overall rank of 68% of the 879 barrios ranked in both and moves 29% two ranks or more; the rebuild on 2017-2021 and on 2020-2024, with the same non-survey inputs, differs for 52% of barrios. tests/test_wcrp_rvi.py checks the method on a small hand-worked example.
source_detail: RVI white paper (Hunter College for FPR, December 2021), an internal FPR document; wcrp_rvi.py
how_to_read: A rank is relative: it says which fifth of barrios a place falls in on the inputs used, not how much need there is.
caveats: A rank compares barrios with each other on the inputs used. It is not a measure of need, risk of harm or eligibility for any program.

Foundation for Puerto Rico runs WCRP in collaboration with the Puerto Rico Department of Housing (PRDOH), with HUD CDBG-DR funds. The WCRP page is published with an 'In review' marker: these values may change, and the page asks search engines not to index it while the marker is on.
Hazards (flood, landslide, sea level rise) are not inputs, as the white paper decided.

name: Community assets of the Comunidades Especiales (WCRP Social Capital Mapping list)
plain: Whether each Comunidad Especial had a community center, a library, an electronic library, a passive park, a sports court, a residents', recreation or crime-prevention association, and a PDI, as the WCRP Social Capital Mapping list records it; counted by municipio.
definition: Nine Yes/No flags of the WCRP Social Capital Mapping list of 711 Comunidades Especiales, as the list writes them: centro_comunal (community center), biblioteca (library), biblioteca_electronica (electronic library), parque_pasivo (passive park), cancha (sports court), asoc_residentes (residents' association), asoc_recreativa (recreation association), asoc_prevencion_crimen (crime-prevention association) and pdi (the list's column PDI, which it does not define). Each flag is 'si', 'no' or 'nd' ('Información No Disponible'). By municipio and for Puerto Rico: listed (rows of the list), matched (rows matched to a polygon of comunidades.geojson), yes.<flag> (rows with 'si') and unknown.<flag> (rows with 'nd'); and for each matched polygon its nine flags as one code (1 yes, 0 no, - not recorded).
unit: count of communities; a flag per community
geography: 78 municipios and Puerto Rico; 710 of the 713 Comunidades Especiales polygons

coverage.frequency: Date not stated: the WCRP Social Capital Mapping list, about 2019-2021, from the Junta de Planificación inventory; no live source

method: wcrp_social.py --import reads the list, restores the municipio names and, where it can, the accented letters the copy lost, and matches each row to a polygon of the same municipio: by the same name once accents, capitals and punctuation are set aside (686 rows), by name and barrio where two polygons share the name (1), or by a clearly closest name in the same barrio (23; listed with enlace = parecido in wcrp_ce_assets.csv for review). One row is not matched (Parcelas Pda. 27, San Juan); 3 polygons have no row. The build counts the flags by municipio over every row, matched or not.
source_detail: COMUNIDADES ESPECIALES.csv, WCRP Social Capital Mapping tool (FPR SharePoint, Community Resiliency Planning); cleaned extract wcrp_ce_assets.csv
how_to_read: Read a count as what the list recorded when it was compiled, not as today's situation. 'Not recorded' is not 'no': about 110 to 130 rows have no information for each flag except PDI.
caveats: The list's date is not stated. It was compiled for the WCRP Social Capital Mapping tool, about 2019-2021, from the Junta de Planificación inventory; assets may have opened or closed since.
The list does not define PDI.
23 rows are matched to a polygon by a close name, not the same name: wcrp_ce_assets.csv marks them (enlace = parecido) so a reviewer can check them.

name: Residents and Comunidades Especiales by municipio, for the WCRP Social Capital summary
plain: For each municipio: its residents (latest Census Bureau estimate), which the WCRP page divides the asset counts by, and how many Comunidades Especiales and housing units in them it has (2006).
definition: population: residents, the latest year of the Census Bureau's Population Estimates in housing_series.json (2025, Vintage 2025), the denominator of the per-1,000 rates of the WCRP page's municipio summary. polygons: the Comunidades Especiales of comunidades.geojson in the municipio. housing_units: the sum of their housing units (viviendas, Junta de Planificación 2006 inventory). The last value of each array is Puerto Rico.
unit: people; communities; housing units

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt by python wcrp_social.py when housing_series.json or comunidades.geojson changes

method: Copied from housing_series.json (population, latest year) and counted from comunidades.geojson by its municipio field. The residents inside a protected area, which the summary divides by the 2020 Census residents, come from exposure_municipio.json.
source_detail: housing_series.json:population; comunidades.geojson:municipio, viviendas
how_to_read: A rate per 1,000 residents compares municipios of different sizes; for small counts (a few stations) a single facility moves the rate a lot.
caveats: The Comunidades Especiales and their housing units describe the 2006 delimitation, not today.
